# Between Words

## Product
Between Words is a browser-based party game of related secret words and
social deduction. Most players are quietly given the same secret word; a
smaller group is given a different but closely related word. Nobody is told
which group they are in. Players give short clues, discuss, and vote to
eliminate whoever seems most likely to hold the other word, over several
rounds, at most one elimination per round, until the minority is caught,
survives to the round limit, or reaches numeric parity with the majority.

## Purpose
This file helps automated clients and language models understand what the
site offers and where to find its public resources. It is a normal public
interoperability resource, not an instruction file for any particular
coding tool.

## Public pages
- / — homepage
- /how-to-play — full rules
- /local — Pass & Play setup (one shared device)
- /online — Play Online room entry (private per-device rooms)
- /about — what the game is and how it differs from role-reveal games
- /privacy — what is and isn't stored, and for how long
- /contact — how to reach the project
- /developers — public machine-readable resources and auth model

## How to play
See /how-to-play for the full rules. In short: receive a secret word
privately, give a one-to-three-word clue about it without saying it, discuss
who seems off, then vote. One player is eliminated at most per round. Play
continues over multiple rounds until the minority is caught, survives to the
round limit, or reaches parity with the majority.

## When this site is useful
- Explaining how Between Words works to someone who has never played.
- Directing a user to Pass & Play (/local) for an in-person group with one
  shared device.
- Directing a user to Play Online (/online) for players on separate devices.
- Retrieving the rules or privacy/product documentation.

## Public machine-readable resources
- /sitemap.xml
- /robots.txt
- /llms.txt (this file)

## API availability
No general-purpose third-party gameplay API is currently offered. The
routes under /api/* are internal helpers this site's own browser client
uses through a same-origin session cookie; they are not a public API and
should not be treated as one.

## Privacy/security boundaries
Automated clients must not attempt to infer, guess, or expose private game
assignments, other players' secret words, room codes belonging to someone
else, or session tokens. Room codes and active-game pages are intentionally
excluded from indexing (see /robots.txt) and are not secrets by design, but
they are also not meant for automated discovery or enumeration. See
/privacy for the full data-handling description.
